task: Control Plane ecosystem chain foundation: connect gate contracts, projected risk, proof obligations, repository relationship mapping and implementation skeleton before code execution.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The Control Plane gates are individually strict but their deterministic knowledge, downstream requirements, phase state and release implications are not yet propagated as one canonical development chain, causing foreseeable failures to be discovered late and forcing avoidable manual reconciliation.
observableOutcomes: Before implementation starts, the active plan exposes one machine-derived implementation skeleton covering repository relationships, applicable gates, downstream obligations and projected release risk.
Every applicable downstream guard requirement that is deterministically knowable from planned scope is visible upstream before code execution rather than first appearing as a later CI failure.
External proof applicability is derived from canonical guard semantics and affected scope so Completion Truth cannot report a locally complete claim while a required external proof is absent.
unresolvedRisks: Some guard semanticInputs are intentionally broad, so initial automatic applicability may expose over-broad contracts that must be corrected at the owning guard rather than suppressed locally.
Atlas cannot infer genuinely new runtime relationships that do not yet exist, so MUST_CREATE declarations require fail-closed reconciliation after the first implementation diff.
Phase-aware execution and lifecycle-only CI optimization depend on a later workflow release unit and are intentionally not activated by this foundation commit.

in: Canonical gate contract and dependency-chain semantics for development orchestration.
Machine-derived implementation skeleton from Atlas relationships plus planned file intent.
Projected Release Risk calculation during planning using the existing production risk policy.
Backward propagation of proof obligations including external proof applicability.
out: No authentication, authorization, tenant, storefront or business-runtime behavior changes.
No weakening of Release Risk Budget, Sentinel, Completion Truth or existing blocking guards.
No CI workflow phase-skipping or lifecycle auto-commit in this first release unit.
No activation or merge of parked workforce AAL2 enforcement.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This change modifies the Control Plane authority that decides what future work may edit, what evidence is required and when a development transaction is considered complete. A false PASS could affect every later subsystem, so the strongest practical assurance profile is required while keeping final production and external proofs independently authoritative.

acceptanceCriteria: The guard registry can declare machine-readable gate dependencies, consumed inputs, produced outputs, applicable phases and proof obligations without creating a second guard authority.
The Development Guard writes changeBaseSha and a machine-derived implementation skeleton before coding, including MUST_EDIT, MAY_EDIT, IMPACTED_READ_ONLY, MUST_CREATE and FORBIDDEN categories.
Plan Before Code evaluates projected Release Risk from planned scope using the canonical release-risk policy and blocks a plan that is predictably over budget before implementation starts.
Plan Before Code produces an ordered applicable gate chain and blocks dependency cycles, missing producers and unresolved downstream obligations.
External completion proof requirements are derived from affected scope and guard semantics in addition to explicit PO completion references, so relevant external proof cannot be omitted accidentally.
Existing blocking gates remain authoritative and final exact-diff Release Risk, exact-head evidence and Completion Truth are not weakened or replaced.
invariants: One canonical guard registry remains the authority for gate identity and dependency semantics.
Atlas and existing domain authorities remain the source of repository relationship truth; the ecosystem layer consumes them rather than duplicating them.
Projected Release Risk is advisory-before-code but blocking when predictably invalid; actual Release Risk remains the final release authority.
Unknown producer, dependency cycle, unknown relationship and stale transaction identity fail closed.
Machine-derivable data is generated upstream and must not require manual re-entry downstream.

failureModes: A downstream guard requires data that an upstream guard already knew but did not persist into the transaction.
The planned file set is already over Release Risk Budget but the block is discovered only after implementation.
A plan-only transaction is interpreted as failed implementation because phase applicability is not represented explicitly.
Completion Truth verifies only locally declared evidence while an applicable external proof is missing.
A new file duplicates an existing canonical capability because repository relationship mapping was not consulted before implementation.
A gate dependency graph contains a cycle or a required input has no authoritative producer.
edgeCases: A planned file does not yet exist and must be represented as MUST_CREATE rather than silently omitted from projection.
A planned rename or deletion must retain old-path dependency information so consumers are reconciled before edit completion.
A broad semantic input pattern may make an external guard applicable; the system must surface the reason instead of hiding it.
A high-risk subsystem projected together with any other substantive subsystem must be split before implementation.
A neutral test or evidence file must not increase release risk while still participating in proof obligations.
A closed lifecycle plan must remain read-only and preserve verified-head ancestry semantics.

alternatives.summary: Patch each observed Stage 1 friction point independently inside its current script.
alternatives.reason: This would preserve the same fragmented knowledge flow and require future missing handoffs to be rediscovered one by one.

alternatives.summary: Build a separate orchestration system beside the existing Control Plane and migrate gates later.
alternatives.reason: A second authority would violate canonical ownership and create exactly the ecosystem fragmentation this work is intended to remove.

alternatives.summary: Extend the existing registry, Atlas consumers and development transaction so current gates form one dependency-aware chain.
alternatives.reason: This reuses proven authorities, makes requirements flow through one transaction and improves the current system without weakening or duplicating any gate.

specialistReviews.finding: The missing capability is orchestration across existing authorities, not another standalone engine.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep guard identity in guard-registry.v1.json and derive the chain from existing Atlas, plan and release policies.

specialistReviews.finding: Projected risk must not become a replacement for exact-diff Release Risk because planned scope can differ from the final diff.
specialistReviews.resolution: Projected risk blocks predictably invalid plans early while scripts/release-risk-budget.mjs remains the final release authority until the later shared-runtime adapter is proven.

specialistReviews.finding: The Stage 1 delay demonstrates a missing-edge class: deterministic downstream obligations were discovered after the phase where they could have prevented rework.
specialistReviews.resolution: Introduce ecosystem integrity findings for missing producer, cycle, late discovery and redundant recomputation, then cover them with one regression suite.

specialistReviews.finding: The plan generator currently leaves transaction identity and many machine-derivable obligations for manual completion.
specialistReviews.resolution: Generate changeBaseSha and the implementation skeleton automatically so operators only supply genuinely human decisions.

challenge.scenario: A plan contains one high-risk auth file and three medium presentation files before any implementation exists.
challenge.finding: Without projected risk the plan can be semantically valid yet guaranteed to fail Release Risk after code is written.
challenge.resolution: Compute projected risk from the planned file envelope and require decomposition before execution when policy would block.

challenge.scenario: A plan-only commit has no implementation diff but CI executes Edit-Time and Truth as if execution were complete.
challenge.finding: The gate result is technically correct but phase-inappropriate and creates a false red development signal.
challenge.resolution: Foundation emits canonical phase applicability; the subsequent CI unit will consume it and represent later gates as not-applicable-yet rather than failed.

challenge.scenario: A Template Factory relevant file changes but the PO Completion Contract forgets to name GUARD-TEMPLATE-FACTORY.
challenge.finding: Local Completion Truth can overclaim because external proof applicability currently depends on manual evidence references.
challenge.resolution: Derive external proof applicability from guard semantic inputs and affected scope, fail closed on missing required evidence, and expose the reason upstream.

challenge.scenario: A new implementation file is planned but does not yet exist in the Atlas node set.
challenge.finding: Current projection can omit the file entirely and therefore cannot tell coding that creation is an explicit obligation.
challenge.resolution: Represent unmatched exact planned paths as MUST_CREATE and reconcile them against the first actual diff.

challenge.scenario: A task edits a file whose consumers require companion changes in an existing canonical module.
challenge.finding: A file-list-only plan can miss the existing related implementation point and create a local workaround.
challenge.resolution: Build the implementation skeleton from Atlas consumers, authorities and semantic route categories before coding starts.

challenge.scenario: Two gate contracts depend on each other's output.
challenge.finding: A naive pipeline can deadlock or rely on incidental execution order.
challenge.resolution: Compile a directed dependency graph and block cycles or unresolved producers before execution authorization.

challenge.scenario: Two gates independently recompute the same deterministic fact and disagree.
challenge.finding: Independent recomputation creates competing truth and makes later diagnostics ambiguous.
challenge.resolution: Name one producer for each canonical transaction datum and require downstream consumers to read the produced value.

challenge.scenario: A broad guard semantic input makes a costly external proof applicable to a seemingly small change.
challenge.finding: Silently suppressing the proof would weaken assurance while blindly accepting the broad pattern can create unnecessary cost.
challenge.resolution: Surface applicability provenance in the plan; if the pattern is over-broad, repair the owning guard contract in a later reviewed change rather than bypassing the proof.

proofPlan: Require Plan Before Code PASS on the plan-only head with exact changeBaseSha, full Known Failure replay scope and no implementation files changed.
Add focused regression coverage for gate-chain ordering, cycle detection, missing producer detection, MUST_CREATE projection and projected risk classification.
Verify external proof applicability is derived from semanticInputs even when the PO Completion Contract omits the external guard identifier.
Run Edit-Time Guard and Incremental Replay after the implementation batch and require no expanded unplanned subsystem or authority.
Require actual Release Risk Budget PASS without changing its thresholds or classification rules.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build on the implementation head.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and preserve external proof as an independent blocking authority where semantically applicable.
Close lifecycle only after the verified implementation head is recorded; workflow optimization is deferred to the dedicated later release unit.

requirements.requirement: The existing Control Plane guards form one dependency-aware chain whose upstream outputs and downstream requirements are machine-readable before implementation.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The change must not create a second guard registry or independent orchestration truth.

requirements.requirement: Before coding, repository relationships and planned intent produce one implementation skeleton covering existing required edits, read-only impacts and explicit new-file obligations.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A planned exact new file must not disappear from the pre-code implementation route.

requirements.requirement: A release scope that is predictably outside the canonical Release Risk Budget is blocked during planning before implementation work begins.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Projected classification must not weaken or fork the canonical production release-risk policy.

requirements.requirement: Applicable downstream and external proof obligations are derived from affected scope so omission from manually authored completion evidence cannot create a false completion claim.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A semantically applicable external blocking guard must not become optional merely because it was omitted from the manual Completion Contract.

notes: Foundation release unit for the accepted Control Plane ecosystem evolution. No business runtime behavior is in scope; later release units will consume the emitted phase, risk and obligation data in CI/lifecycle/release tooling.
